answer: Routing-path diversity enforcement: every identity must prove its traffic traverses a distinct autonomous system, verified against public BGP tables, and committees are sampled so no two members share an AS or carrier. A sybil farm on one cloud host sits in a single AS like a lone oasis in a canyon: its clones all leak one traceroute signature at each dawn validation round and are rejected as a cluster. Attacker cost: each clone needs rented infrastructure in a separate AS with unique egress IPs, so copy-paste sybils become a multi-jurisdiction procurement burden with negligible voting gain.
